body: And what that puts downstream of it.

body: The owner's calibration.

title: Home is the session list
body: With a pinned banner for open decisions.

title: Sessions are supervised through tmux
body: Crash-survival free; a terminal can still attach.

title: Decision detail is generated on demand
body: One paragraph up front; deeper costs tokens only when asked.

title: Phone surfaces show only the recent
body: ~1 hour, then the archive.

title: Invisibility is taught once
body: First run and empty state, never permanent chrome.

title: Mustur is written in Go
body: The case survived removing the tooling argument.

title: The product stores in SQLite, exports to markdown
body: Insert-only by trigger; the export is the audit surface.

title: Identifiers are project, role, serial
body: Records are named MUS-D-0001: a three-letter project prefix, a role letter, a four-digit serial. Permanent, sortable, and unique once a second project onboards.

title: The store holds records, the contract files keep their prose
body: Every decision, milestone, finding and investigation that already existed is addressable in the store; the long rationale stays in the file that holds it, cited by link rather than copied.

title: The export is committed under records
body: The markdown export lives at records/ and is committed, so record history is in git and reviewable in a diff by someone who does not run the binary.

title: One record shape, not a table per kind
body: Every module role and every routing row uses the same record shape, so a new kind costs no second insert path, export path or audit path.

title: The SQLite driver is pure Go
body: modernc.org/sqlite rather than the cgo binding, because the static single binary was already decided and cgo would end it.

title: What the mandate keeps from the fixture, and what it does not
body: The tool keeps the name and arguments the milestone 1 stub carried, and the clause in the context file is the fixture's wording. Three things differ and the entry names all three: two optional arguments, a sentence for when the tool is absent, and the transport — the fixture was stdio, where the tool is always there.

title: Four of StrucGu's five roles are implemented, and the repository adopts five modules
body: Corrects MUS-D-0009. The product implements four module roles as record kinds; triage-rule describes a document rather than records and has none. The repository itself adopts five modules, work-units among them since milestone 2.

title: A milestone is read by agents that did not build it
body: Owner-set. Three reviewers spawned fresh per milestone — this milestone's done-when, the shipped claims, and workflow.md's own gates — each given the milestone, the branch and the contract and never the builder's report. They change nothing; findings are dispositioned in the pull request.

data.value: LinkCtrl's phase loop, with three deliberate differences
